s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis
salient_findings: Chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression on ECG
key_facts: Subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, dry cough, and sinus congestion 4 days prior to presentation
3 hours of substernal pressure that resolved spontaneously the day prior to presentation
Constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein
Initial serum troponin I level of 6.18 ng/mL
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin and inflammatory markers with normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis, elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin and inflammatory markers with normal echocardiogram results

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin, but less likely given normal coronary arteries and young age

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain with radiation to the jaw and diaphoresis, elevated troponin, but less likely given lack of stressor

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pressure, elevated troponin, and ST-segment elevations on ECG, along with signs of inflammation (elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein) and normal coronary arteries, suggests an inflammatory process affecting both the myocardium and pericardium.

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: While pericarditis could explain some symptoms, the elevated troponin level suggests myocardial involvement.

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: Myocarditis could explain the elevated troponin and some ECG changes, but the presence of PR-segment elevation in lead aVR and ST-segment elevations in leads II, III, and aVF also suggest pericardial involvement.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on angiography make this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and diagnostic findings do not typically match those of takotsubo cardiomyopathy, which often involves significant left ventricular dysfunction not seen here.
